title: I spent 150+ hours making a rogue lite beat 'em up for myself, I'd like to know if it's too hard.  Empty Fist Taro (Claude for coding/GPT for Image Assets)
author: Agreeable-Gap5500
selftext:
I tried to make a game before in Godot in like 2023. It was an *unmitigated disaster*. I used to code in PHP many years ago but I had all but forgotten it. I used to draw as a kid but I was pretty terrible.  So imagine my joy to learn that in the Lords' year of 2026 I could use AI to make a game on both fronts. 

**Backstory:** I learned about Google Playground a month ago and I tried it.  It wasn't so great.  Single prompting a game, and then using prompts to hone changes wasn't well done.  I was trying to get Claude to help me write better prompts, but nothing seemed to work.  Then Claude literally wrote: "I can try making it for you." 

And so in HTML5 I started a slow and iterative process of "vibe coding" a game.  At first a sprite sheet in GPT along with a simple pixel background, then eventually to Claude developing a custom cutter tool and regression testing script.  Then moving the project into GitHub, and then eventually getting it uploaded into Itch.io.  It's been a REALLY fun and exciting process, and I still have a million ideas for it.  The work flow was to introduce a new and different mechanic, or enemy, and then to test after each implementation.  Claude would run regression tests to make sure it passed, I did the playthrough to see if it made sense, or if it needed to be tweaked.  (I'm sure EVERYONE here does it like this to some extent)  

The concept is straightforward.  It's a single plane side scrolling beat 'em up. (Think the original Nintendo Kung-Fu) But I wanted to have command moves and parries like Street Fighter (which uses ki).  I also wanted it to have a rogue-like replay-ability and meta progression.  There's only 3 levels, a day and night stage for each level, and 4 combat waves per stage.  Between stages you have a shrine where you can spend your run tokens for moves.  These moves unlock in the dojo every time you die, and the persistent meta currency earned every run is Jade.  Death = Unlocked Moves, Jade = Purchases those moves to appear in mid level shrines.  And you collect tokens off the enemies you beat up.  Rinse. Repeat.  Try to complete all of the Dojo purchases.

I really enjoy playing it, and I've made a mobile version I can play when I'm out and about (it's way harder on a virtual controller) And I've sent it to friends and family to play.  But they all tell me it's too hard.  I tried posting on here a week ago hoping others would play it, but I'm having a hard time getting anyone to try it out.  **I don't plan on selling it, just keeping it free and constantly adding updates and changes to suit my whims, but I wouldn't mind some honest feedback.**  ***Is it too hard?  Is it unwieldly? Do the controls suck?  Does it take too long to get good? (As a rogue lite, it's kind of supposed to be hard)***

Now that I have a base game, adding new features is pretty fun.  For example, for Thanksgiving 2026 I added a turkey (7Face) that has a 33% spawn rate, and he gets spooked if you do a special move near him.  HOWEVER if you have the air fireball, you can actually try to hit him and get a fully roasted turkey dinner that fills all health and ki.   

![img](d9ce2ye6eo3i1 "7Face the Karate Turkey")

Anyway, I'm having a blast making this and I'm going to continue dumping hours into adding more features and functionality.  I think in a world where many people really like this game, I might try to Kickstarter getting real artists and musicians and replacing all of the AI assets with real human-made art/music, and I could use the Kickstarter to pay them all.  But if people just LIKE it for what it is, I'm happy to continue making more updates and features.  (Like couch co-op, unlockable players, more stages, harder bosses, etc.) I just want to know if people like it, and I can build a community around developing it.  

Thanks for reading this giant post and I'm happy to talk about my process further, or if you want to play the game check out the [itch.io](http://itch.io) link: (It's gamepad compatible but can be played on keyboard/mouse and mobile) 

[**https://melzworld.itch.io/empty-fist-taro**](https://melzworld.itch.io/empty-fist-taro)

P.S. Parry is the most important mechanic.  *Please parry often.*  

  
I post updates a lot, but I'd really love feedback, and even a rating for it on itch if you're feeling generous.  

  
*Happy Thanksgiving!*
